_about: Every number in the video comes from this file: value + 95% interval (Wilson for fractions unless noted) + n + scheme spread (V4: production vs half step, in points) + the raw file. Generated by sim/run.py results. Percentages are in percent.

E1.angles: node, argument of pericentre, mean anomaly uniform 0-360 deg
E1.seed: numpy.random.default_rng(2_000_001), arrays drawn in the order a, e, inc, node, peri, M

sampling_box.E2: E1 ids 0-99,999, 843 laps of each giant

T_MAIN_YR.definition: length of the main run; exactly 4214 laps of the giant = 49999.8 yr. Fallback used: False (projected 73.9 min at 50,000 yr, limit 85)

LAPS.definition: laps of the giant in the main run (P_G = 11.8652 yr)

LOST_PCT.definition: E1: share of the 1,000,000 test planets lost (ENCOUNTER, INWARD or OUTWARD) by the end
LOST_PCT.spread_note: V4 change of the lost fraction at 10,000 yr with half step and half check interval (20,000 planets)

SURV_PCT.definition: E1: share not lost at the end (never entered the Hill sphere, never left the disk; not the same as still on the starting orbit, see details.e1.survivors_changed)

SURV_COUNT.definition: E1: number of test planets not lost at the end: never entered the Hill sphere, never left the disk (interval from LOST_PCT). Not the same as still on the starting orbit, see details.e1.survivors_changed

LOST_1LAP_PCT.definition: E1: share lost by t = 11.9 yr

LOST_100YR_PCT.definition: E1: share lost by t = 100.0 yr

LOST_1KYR_PCT.definition: E1: share lost by t = 1000.0 yr

LOST_10KYR_PCT.definition: E1: share lost by t = 10002.3 yr (843 laps; the dial runs' length)

HALF_LOSS_YR.definition: E1: median loss time of all lost planets (half of all losses of the run had happened by then); times are on the event-test grid (P_G/15 = 0.79 yr); interval: bootstrap

LATE_LOSS_PCT.definition: E1: share of ALL test planets lost in the last fifth of the run (t > 40000 yr)

ENC_PCT.definition: E1: share of the LOST planets whose event was entering the giant's Hill sphere (ENCOUNTER)

OUTWARD_N.definition: E1: number of OUTWARD exits (includes the ARTIFACT_N planets with an unphysical kick; OUTWARD_GENUINE_N is the rest)

ARTIFACT_N.definition: E1: planets with an unphysical kick. OUTWARD exits with (a) an element sample with a <= 0 (afin <= 0, amin <= 0 or emax >= 1) or (b) a last element sample (at most P_G/3 = 3.96 yr before the event) whose far point a(1+e) was under 20 au although the event test then found the planet beyond 52 au. Cause: a deep pass by the point-mass giant not resolved by the fixed WHFast step. They are counted as lost, which they would be anyway (they went deep inside the Hill sphere); only their class (OUTWARD instead of ENCOUNTER) and their recorded eccentricity are wrong

OUTWARD_GENUINE_N.definition: E1: OUTWARD exits without the ARTIFACT_N planets

REACH_PCT.definition: share of the sampled disc whose starting ellipse can touch the giant's Hill sphere (Q >= q_G - r_H and q <= Q_G + r_H, tilt ignored); exact count of the starting conditions, our own arithmetic (draw in --muted)

REACH_SURV_PCT.definition: E1: survival of the planets IN reach

OUT_OF_REACH_LOST_N.definition: E1: lost planets that started out of reach

OUT_OF_REACH_LOST_PCT.definition: E1: share of the LOST planets that started out of reach

REACH_LANE_WIDTH.definition: width of the 'simple guess' lane for round orbits: 4.595 to 5.813 au [CALC]

LANE_IN_AU.definition: E1, round orbits (e0 < 0.05): inner lane edge = centre of the first of 3 adjacent 0.04-au windows that all have survival below 50%, walking from 2.5 au inside the giant toward it in 0.02-au steps (for E1 the older first-window rule gives the same edge); interval: bootstrap

LANE_OUT_AU.definition: E1, round orbits: outer lane edge (same walk from 2.5 au outside)

LANE_ONLY_LOST_PCT.definition: E1: lost share of all planets (any starting shape) starting between LANE_IN_AU and LANE_OUT_AU

TROJAN_SURV_PCT.definition: E1: survival of planets starting with |a0 - a_G| < 0.25 au and 30-90 deg ahead of or behind the giant (mean longitude)

COORB_OTHER_SURV_PCT.definition: E1: same, but within 30 deg of the giant or of the point opposite it

TROJAN_SURV_N.definition: E1: number of co-orbital (|a0 - a_G| < 0.25 au) survivors, all phases

HILDA_SURV_PCT.definition: E1: survival for a0 in 3.93-4.01 au (3:2), all e0

HILDA_NEIGHBOR_PCT.definition: E1: survival for a0 in 3.80-3.93 and 4.01-4.14 au

HILDA_INSIDE_PCT.definition: E1: survival for a0 in 3.80-3.93 au (just inside the 3:2 bin), all e0

HILDA_OUTSIDE_PCT.definition: E1: survival for a0 in 4.01-4.14 au (just outside the 3:2 bin), all e0

STRETCH_31.definition: E1: mean of (max e - e0) in the 0.01-au bin at the 3:1 peak (2.505 au)

STRETCH_BG.definition: E1: median of the bins 0.05-0.15 au from the 3:1 peak

INWARD_31_N.definition: E1: INWARD exits that started within 0.03 au of 2.502 au

RES_PEAKS_AU.definition: E1: centre of the 0.01-au bin with the largest mean eccentricity gain within 0.03 au of each resonance

UNDER_RESOLVED_N.definition: E1: planets whose osculating pericentre time q^1.5 fell below 12 integration steps at any element sample (resolution warning; most of them were lost soon after)

LOST_BASE10K_PCT.definition: E2 baseline: the 100,000 dial planets around the Jupiter copy, lost by 843 laps (10,002 yr), read from E1
LOST_BASE10K_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_E00_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 1 Jupiter, eccentricity 0; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_E00_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_E010_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 1 Jupiter, eccentricity 0.1; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_E010_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_E023_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 1 Jupiter, eccentricity 0.23; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_E023_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_E04_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 1 Jupiter, eccentricity 0.4; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_E04_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_M01_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 0.1 Jupiter, eccentricity 0.0487; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_M01_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_M03_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 0.3 Jupiter, eccentricity 0.0487; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_M03_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_M3_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 3 Jupiter, eccentricity 0.0487; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_M3_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

LOST_M10_PCT.definition: E2: lost by 843 laps of the giant, giant mass 10 Jupiter, eccentricity 0.0487; the same 100,000 planets
LOST_M10_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

MASS_RATIO.definition: LOST_M10_PCT / LOST_M01_PCT (interval from the two Wilson intervals, conservative)
MASS_RATIO.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

E04_MINUS_BASE.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

TROJAN_E04_PCT.definition: E2 e = 0.4: survival of planets starting 30-90 deg ahead of or behind the giant with |a0 - a_G| < 0.25 au
TROJAN_E04_PCT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

EDGE_SURV_E04_IN.definition: E2 e = 0.4: survival of planets starting in the innermost 0.3 au of the disc (1.561-1.861 au)
EDGE_SURV_E04_IN.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

EDGE_SURV_E04_OUT.definition: E2 e = 0.4: survival in the outermost 0.3 au (10.108-10.408 au)
EDGE_SURV_E04_OUT.source: raw/e2_<case>.npz; baseline from raw/e1_planets.npz (ids 0-99,999, t <= 843 laps)

FATE_BOUND_PCT.definition: E3: share of the 1000 re-run lost planets with fate BOUND by 200000 yr (IAS15, one planet per simulation, physical radii)

FATE_GIANT_PCT.definition: E3: share of the 1000 re-run lost planets with fate HIT_GIANT by 200000 yr (IAS15, one planet per simulation, physical radii)

FATE_EJECT_PCT.definition: E3: share of the 1000 re-run lost planets with fate EJECTED by 200000 yr (IAS15, one planet per simulation, physical radii)

FATE_STAR_PCT.definition: E3: share of the 1000 re-run lost planets with fate HIT_STAR by 200000 yr (IAS15, one planet per simulation, physical radii)

E3_ENTERED_PCT.definition: E3: share of the IAS15 re-runs that entered the giant's Hill sphere at least once (independent check of the WHFast classification)

ORBIT_CHANGED_PCT.definition: E3: among re-runs that entered the Hill sphere, share whose a differs from the start by > 5% or e by > 0.05, 100 yr after the first entry (impact/ejection before that counts as changed)

PERIOD_SIM_YR.definition: V1: giant's period in the simulation (fit over 50,000 yr, dt = P/60); Kepler value 11.86516 yr

JACOBI_ERR.definition: V2: median over planets of the largest relative change of the Jacobi constant (circular giant, 1,000 laps, planets that stayed outside 2 Hill radii)

LIBRATION_YR.definition: V7: median libration period of 2,000 Trojan test planets (interval = interquartile range, not a CI)

SCHEME_AGREEMENT_PCT.definition: V4: share of 20,000 planets with the same lost/not-lost outcome at production settings and with half step and half check interval (10,000 yr)

SCHEME_SPREAD.definition: V4: change of the lost fraction (half step minus production) at 10,000 yr. The two runs differ in `discordant` single outcomes that nearly cancel; the interval is the paired 95% interval of the difference, and it, not the value, is the precision (say 'less than 0.2 points')

ZONE_EXPONENT_OUTER.definition: V5: the same fit on the OUTER lane edge (reported, not part of the test)

IAS15_AGREEMENT_PCT.definition: V3: share of 5,000 planets with the same lost/not-lost outcome in WHFast (production) and IAS15 over 5,000 yr

ZONE_EXPONENT.definition: V5: fitted exponent of the inner lane edge distance (a_G - edge)/a_G against giant mass mu (4 masses, circular giant, round test orbits); published 2/7 = 0.286. Interval: refit with edges drawn from their bootstrap intervals

ZONE_COEFF.definition: V5: fitted coefficient (published 1.3 Wisdom 1980; 1.57 Murray & Dermott fit)

N_PASSED.definition: validation tests passed of V1-V9 (V6 on the main run)

LOST_FRACTION_SPOKEN.definition: nearest of quarter/third/half/two thirds/three quarters to LOST_PCT, only if within 2 points + |scheme spread|; null = say the number

MASS_RATIO_SPOKEN.definition: write at script lock from MASS_RATIO = 3.53 (interval 3.47-3.59)

ZONE_EXPONENT_DIGITS.definition: two digits after 'zero point' of ZONE_EXPONENT

EJECT_RUN.definition: E3/E4: id of the replayed ejection (the EJECTED planet with the median ejection time)

EJECT_REPLAY_LINE.definition: [RD-REPLAY] to be written by a person after reading the track; measured facts of the track are in `facts`

REAL_N_TOTAL.definition: all asteroids (sb-kind=a) in the JPL SBDB on REAL_DATA_DATE

REAL_N_BOX.definition: asteroids with 1.56 <= a <= 10.41 au (our disc's range)

REAL_TROJAN_N.definition: asteroids of orbit class TJN (Jupiter Trojan)

REAL_HILDA_RANGE_N.definition: asteroids with 3.7 <= a < 4.2 au (a distance range, not a resonance test)

REAL_DATA_DATE.definition: UTC retrieval date of the cached download

LAPS_SPOKEN.definition: spoken form, written at script lock from the numeric placeholder

SURV_COUNT_SPOKEN.definition: spoken form, written at script lock from the numeric placeholder

TOTAL_PLANETS_SPOKEN.definition: spoken form, written at script lock from the numeric placeholder

TOTAL_STEPS_SPOKEN.definition: spoken form, written at script lock from the numeric placeholder

WALL_SPOKEN.definition: spoken form, written at script lock from the numeric placeholder

TOTAL_PLANETS.definition: all test-planet runs of all experiments and validation tests (WHFast chunk planets + IAS15 single-planet runs + replays); a planet re-run in another test counts again

TOTAL_STEPS.definition: WHFast planet-steps (one test planet advanced by one step) of all WHFast runs + IAS15 steps of all single-planet runs (replays not counted)

WALL_MIN.definition: wall-clock minutes of all stages (sum of raw/stage_times.json), Mac mini M4, 10 worker processes, machine shared with other jobs

S06_p2_crossing.rule: >= 80% of BOUND carry the crossing flag

S06_p2_order.rule: name the fates in order of size

S07_p4_hilda.rule: HILDA >= NEIGHBOR + 10 points and intervals do not overlap

S08_p3_resonances.rule: name only resonances with a genuine peak (V6)

S09_p4_both_edges.rule: edges < 98% at e=0.4 and >= 99.5% at baseline

DIAL_FLAT.rule: shape dial flat if LOST_E04 - LOST_BASE10K < 5 points

S10_p2_rounder_kept_more.rule: LOST_E023 - BASE > scheme spread and paired 95% interval excludes 0

S13_p1_shrinks.rule: from e 0.05 to 0.23: inner edge inward, outer edge outward, Trojan survival down, each beyond its interval

survivors_changed.note: survivors (never entered the Hill sphere, never left the disk) whose LAST element sample differs from the start; 'not lost' is therefore not 'on the starting orbit'

lane_survivors.note: survivors (any starting shape) that started between LANE_IN_AU and LANE_OUT_AU

numerical_artifacts.rule: OUTWARD exits with (a) an element sample with a <= 0 (afin <= 0, amin <= 0 or emax >= 1) or (b) a last element sample (at most P_G/3 = 3.96 yr before the event) whose far point a(1+e) was under 20 au although the event test then found the planet beyond 52 au. Cause: a deep pass by the point-mass giant not resolved by the fixed WHFast step. They are counted as lost, which they would be anyway (they went deep inside the Hill sphere); only their class (OUTWARD instead of ENCOUNTER) and their recorded eccentricity are wrong
numerical_artifacts.effect: none on LOST_PCT or any spoken number: they are lost either way. OUTWARD_N and ENC_PCT are left as classified; the stretching profile and e_gain exclude them

e2_lane_edges.rule: round orbits (e0 < 0.05), the same 100,000 test planets, 843 laps (about 10,000 yr): centre of the first of 3 adjacent 0.04-au windows (about 76 planets each) that all have survival below 50%, walking in 0.02-au steps from 2.5 au inside / outside the giant (2.70 and 7.70 au) toward it. An edge AT 2.70 or 7.70 au means the lane already reaches the start of the walk: a limit, not an edge

bound_not_crossing.note: still-bound planets whose orbit at year 200,000 does not touch the giant's Hill sphere (one snapshot of an osculating orbit, not a prediction): most still pass close by

v6.rule: each of 3:1, 5:2, 2:1 must have its highest bin within 0.03 au of the Kepler distance; because that is true by construction, we also require a genuine peak: highest bin within 0.10 au and >= 1.5 x the background
